questions.q:
Match List I with List II

List - I List - II
A Surface tension I. $kgm^{- 1}s^{- 1}$
B Pressure II. $kgms^{- 1}$
C Viscosity III. $kgm^{- 1}s^{- 2}$
D Impulse IV. $kgs^{- 2}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) Surface tension is related to force and length as $S = \dfrac{F}{l} = \dfrac{MLT^{- 2}}{L} = MT^{- 2}$

$= kgs^{- 2}$~(IV)

(B) Pressure is related to~force and area as~$P = \dfrac{F}{A}$

~$= \dfrac{MLT^{- 2}}{L^{2}} = kgm^{- 1}s^{- 2}$~ (III)

(C) Viscosity in terms of force, area and velocity gradient is given by $η = \dfrac{F}{A\left(\dfrac{d v}{d x}\right)} = \dfrac{MLT^{- 2}}{L^{2}\left(\dfrac{LT^{- 1}}{L}\right)}$

$= ML^{- 1}T^{- 1} = kgm^{- 1}s^{- 1}$~(I)

(D) Impulse is related to force and time of application as~$J = ∫ Fdt = MLT^{- 2} \times T$

$= MLT^{- 1} = kgms^{- 1}$& (II).

So& A-(IV), B-(III), C-(I), D-(II)

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled as Reason (R)

Assertion (A) : Time period of oscillation of a liquid drop depends on surface tension \left(S\right)$, if density of the liquid is $ρ$ and radius of the drop is $r$, then $T = K\sqrt{\dfrac{ρr^{3}}{S\dfrac{3}{2}}}$ is dimensionally correct, where $K$ is dimensionless.

Reason (R) : Using dimensional analysis we get R.H.S. having different dimension than that of time period. In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

$
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

Using dimensional analysis for the given equation,

$T = K\sqrt{\dfrac{ρr^{3}}{S\dfrac{3}{2}}}$

$⇒ \left[K\right] = \dfrac{ \left[T\right]$\$left[S^{\dfrac{3}{4}}\right]}{ \left[{ρ}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\right]\llleft[r^{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right]} ⇒ \left[$K\right] = \dfrac{ \left[$T\right]\left[M^{\dfrac{3}{4}}T^{- \dfrac{3}{2}}\r$right]}${\l$left[M^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$L^{- $\dfrac{3}{2}}\right] \left[$L^{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right]}⇒ \left[K\right] = $\l$left[M\dfrac{1}{4}$T^{- $\dfrac{1}{2}}\right]$

Therefore,~$K$~is not dimensionless. Hence, Assertion is false.

For dimensional validity of the given equation,~$K$~can not be dimensionless. If it is dimensionless then

Dimensions of L.H.S ≠ Dimensions of R.H.S

$∴$ \text{ and } Option (D) is correct.

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Astronomical unit (Au), Parsec (Pc) and Light year (ly) are units for measuring astronomical distances.
Statement II : Au < Parsec (Pc) < ly
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statements I and Statements II are incorrect
Statements I is correct but Statements II is incorrect
Both Statements I and Statements II are correct
Statements I is incorrect but Statements II is correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Astronomical unit denotes& roughly the distance from Earth to the Sun. Parsec is a unit of length used to measure the large distances to astronomical objects outside the Solar System.& A light-year& is another large unit of length used to express astronomical distances.

The relation between these units are as follows:

$1\text{Parsec} = 2 \times {10}^{5}Au$

$1Au = 1 .58 \times {10}^{- 5}ly$

Thus,~$1Au < \text{ly} < \text{Parsec}$.

Hence,& Statements I is true but Statements II is false.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

$\begin{cases} & \text{List-I} & & \text{List-II} \\ \text{A.} & \text{Coefficient of viscosity} & \text{I.} & \left[{ML}^{2}T^{- 2}\right] \\ \text{B.} & \text{Surface Tension} & \text{II.} & \left[{ML}^{2}T^{- 1}\right] \\ \text{C.} & \text{Angular momentum} & \text{III.} & \left[{ML}^{- 1}T^{- 1}\right] \\ \text{D.} & \text{Rotational kinetic energy} & \text{IV.} & \left[{ML}^{0}T^{- 2}\right]\end{cases}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Boltzmann constant $k$: $E = k T \Rightarrow [k] = \dfrac{[ML^2T^{-2}]}{[K]} = [ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}]$

Stefan's constant $\sigma$: $\dfrac{E}{At} = \sigma T^4 \Rightarrow [\sigma] = \dfrac{[ML^2T^{-2}]}{[L^2][T][K^4]} = [ML^0T^{-3}K^{-4}]$

Planck's constant $h$: $E = h\nu \Rightarrow [h] = \dfrac{[ML^2T^{-2}]}{[T^{-1}]} = [ML^2T^{-1}]$

Gravitational constant $G$: $F = \dfrac{Gm_1m_2}{r^2} \Rightarrow [G] = \dfrac{[MLT^{-2}][L^2]}{[M^2]} = [M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}]$

Thus, A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.q: If momentum$( P )$, area~$( A )$ and time $( T )$ are taken to be the fundamental quantities then the dimensional formula for energy is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let dimension formula of energy will be

$E = A^{a}T^{b}P^{c}$
$P = M^{1}L^{1}T^{- 1}$
$A = L^{2}$
$T = T^{1}$
$M^{1}L^{2}T^{- 2} = M^{C}L^{2a + c}T^{b - c}$
by comparison $C = 1. . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$
$2a + c = 2. . . . . . \left(2\right)$
$b - c = - 2. . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$
$c = 1, a = 1 / 2, b = - 1$
$E = A^{1 / 2}T^{- 1}P^{1}

$

questions.q:
Applying the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, determine which one is correct,
where $T$ is time period, $G$ is gravitational constant, $M$ is mass, $r$ is radius of orbit.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to principle of homogeneity dimension of LHS should be equal to dimensions of RHS so option (3) is correct.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{T}^2=\frac{4 \pi^2 \mathrm{r}^3}{\mathrm{GM}} \\
& {\left[\mathrm{T}^2\right]=\frac{\left[\mathrm{L}^3\right]}{\left[\mathrmM^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right][\mathrm{M}]}}
\end{aligned}$
(Dimension of $\mathrm{G}$ is  \left[\mathrmM^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]$ )
\left[\mathrm{T}^2\right]=\frac{  \left[\mathrm{L}^3\right]}{\left[\mathrm{L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]}=\left[\mathrm{T}^2\right]$

Match List I with List II

List I List II
A Torque I $kgm^{– 1}s^{– 2}$
B Energy density II $kgms^{– 1}$
C Pressure gradient III $kgm^{– 2}s^{– 2}$
D Impulse IV $kgm^{2}s^{– 2}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Unit of force is written as,& $kgms^{- 2}$.

Now, torque can be written as,~$τ = Fs$~therefore its unit can be written as~$kgm^{2}s^{– 2}$.

Pressure is given by,~$P = \dfrac{F}{A}$, therefore unit of pressure will be~$kgm^{- 1}s^{- 2}$.

Now, pressure gradient is given by ratio of pressure and distance, so its unit will be~$kgm^{- 2}s^{- 2}$.

Impulse is given by product of force and time, so its unit will be~$kgms^{- 1}$.

As we know unit of torque and energy is the same, therefore energy density can written as~$= \dfrac{energy}{volume} = kgm^{- 1}s^{– 2}$.

questions.q: Which of the following combinations has the dimension of electrical resistance $( {ϵ}_{0}$ is the permittivity of vacuum and ${\mu}_{0}$ is the permeability of vacuum)?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\left[\text{Resistance}\right]\text{=}\dfrac{\left[\text{Volt}\right]}{\left[\text{Ampere}\right]} = \dfrac{\left[M{L}^{2}{T}^{- 3}{A}^{- 1}\right]}{\left[A\right]} = \left[M{L}^{2}{T}^{- 3}{A}^{- 2}\right]$
We know, ${\mu}_{0} = \left[ML{T}^{- 2}{A}^{- 2}\right]{ε}_{0} = {M}^{- 1}{L}^{- 3}{T}^{4}{A}^{2}$
Hence,
$\sqrt{\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{{ε}_{0}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\left[{\mu}_{0}\right]}{\left[{ε}_{0}\right]}} = {\left[\dfrac{\left[ML{T}^{- 2}{A}^{- 2}\right]}{\left[{M}^{- 1}{L}^{- 3}{T}^{4}{A}^{2}\right]}\right]}^{1 / 2}$
$= {\left[{M}^{2}{L}^{4}{T}^{- 6}{A}^{- 4}\right]}^{1 / 2} = M{L}^{2}{T}^{- 3}{A}^{- 2}$

questions.q: Electric field in a certain region is given by& $\overset{→}{E} = \left(\dfrac{A}{x2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{B}{y3}\overset{^}{j}\right). The SI unit of $A$ and $B$ are :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{E} = \dfrac{A}{x2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{B}{y3}\overset{^}{j}$

Here, the units of ~$\dfrac{A}{x2}$~and~$\dfrac{B}{y3}$~is equal to unit of electric field.

The unit of electric field is~$NC^{- 1}$.

So, the SI unit of $A$ is \left[\dfrac{A}{x2}\right] = NC^{- 1} ⇒ \left[A\right] = Nm^{2}C^{- 1}$

And~the SI unit of $B$~is~\left[\dfrac{B}{y3}\right] = NC^{- 1} ⇒ \left[B\right] = Nm^{3}C^{- 1}$

questions.q: If momentum  \left[P\right]$, area  \left[A\right]$ and time  \left[T\right]$ are taken as fundamental quantities, then the dimensional formula for coefficient of viscosity is$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

We know, Viscosity$=$Pascal$‐$second

Let~ \left[η\right] =P^{x}A^{y}T^{z} = \left[M^{1}L^{- 1}T^{- 1}\right]$

$⇒ \left[M^{1}L^{+ 1}T^{- 1}\$right]x\left[$L^{2}\right]y\left[T^{1}\right]z = M^{1}L^{- 1}T^{- 1}$

$⇒ M^{x}L^{+ x + 2y}T^{- x + z} = M^{1}L^{- 1}T^{- 1}$

From above, we have~

$x = 1x + 2y = - 1 - x + z = - 1$

Solving above three equations, we get~

$y = - 1$~and~$z = 0$

So, Viscosity $= \left[P^{1}A^{- 1}T^{0}\right]$
